request.spec:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The tree export works: `bin/e2e` passed all 4 tests, the tree export test plus the three longer scenarios.

There's a new "Export the tree's people (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-tree"`) next to the other export buttons. It downloads `tree.csv` with the header `sheet,name,grade,due-total`. Rows list the loaded sheet's people first, in list order, then the people of the other sheets in its tree, by sheet id.

It uses the tree search the server already has, run with blank search text so it returns everyone. That search reads from the store, so the file shows what's stored now. Each row has the person's grade on their own sheet's today and their due-total as that sheet shows it, or `n/a` when there is none.

The only file changed is `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. No server or stored-data changes were needed.

Retired people are included in the export, because the tree search doesn't leave them out. That matches the existing people export.
